title: Introduce cascade-moderator: probe-driven soft-stop and tenant taper to prevent KV-miss cascades
author: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Context: On 2026-02-10 we observed a tenant-driven cascade where a sudden burst of KV-cache misses (from a model rollout) amplified upstream latency and triggered aggressive circuit flips in regional routers. The blast radius was amplified by synchronous admission logic that immediately rejected requests, which in turn overloaded fallbacks and caused retry storms. Motivation: introduce a lightweight, probe-driven 'cascade-moderator' that (1) detects early resurgence of KV-miss-driven slowpaths using a low-volume probe, (2) applies a temporary, smoothly decaying 'soft-stop' to tenant acceptance rates rather than an immediate hard reject, and (3) exposes observability hooks and safe toggles for rapid rollback. This is a targeted reliability hotfix: it reduces SLO breach windows during KV-pressure events without changing tenant prioritization or introducing persistent state.

What this PR does (summary): - runtime/cascade_moderator.go: new controller that schedules background probes, computes a KV-miss resurgence score with exponential smoothing, and publishes a tenant-level taper factor (0.0-1.0) to the admission pipeline. - runtime/admission_integration.go: integrates the taper factor into admission decision path; taper is applied as early, low-cost probabilistic admission (fast path) to avoid blocking. - runtime/cascade_moderator_test.go & integration fixture: unit and small e2e test harness that simulates KV miss bursts and verifies graceful SLO degradation (no circuit flips within the window). - telemetry/metrics.yaml: new metrics and tag conventions (cascade.moderator.resurgence, cascade.moderator.taper, cascade.moderator.probe_latency). - console/alerts.yaml: temporary alert rule to surface prolonged >30s taper windows for on-call inspection. - docs/ops/cascade-moderator.md: ops runbook (probe tuning, rollback steps, canary scope). - deploy/k8s/redwood-configmap.yaml: config knobs exposed (probe-interval, smoothing-alpha, max-taper-duration) with safe defaults. - hotfixes/2026-02-15/rollback.sh: one-line toggle to disable cascade-moderator via configmap and restart controller with zero downtime.

Behavior and safety properties: - Probe-based detection: probes are small, randomized requests that exercise KV path; they are rate-limited and never exceed a configured low QPS per region. - Soft-stop taper: when resurgence score crosses threshold, we compute a taper that probabilistically reduces accepted requests for affected tenants; taper decays exponentially over a configured warmup period. This avoids abrupt circuit flips and reduces retry amplification. - No persistent tenant state: taper is ephemeral and derived from real-time telemetry; controllers have built-in max-duration and emergency cutoff to ensure recovery. - Observability-first: new metrics and tracing annotations added to correlate taper windows with downstream SLOs and KV miss rates. - Rollback: disabling the feature is a single configmap update; an emergency kill switch is wired to the operator namespace for on-call use.

Testing and rollout plan: - Unit tests and a small e2e in CI simulate common KV-miss patterns (steady, burst, and oscillatory). - Staged rollout: enable in canary region A for 24h with conservative thresholds, collect metrics, then expand to three regions. - On-call runbook includes metric thresholds and rollback steps. - Post-merge: a short-lived dashboard will be deployed for the incident review window.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation code + unit tests - [x] Integrations updated - [x] Metrics and alerts added - [x] Ops runbook added - [x] k8s toggle + rollback script - [x] CI green

Related work: this complements ENG-3973 (KV pressure observability) and is orthogonal to the tenant-surge-fuse work; it is intentionally scoped as a runtime emergency mitigation rather than a long-term admission policy redesign.
